items.text: Vault shell geometry stands straight along the particle's long axis in each published account, said there as vertical staves of stacked domains, a quasi-linear spoke structure, three tryptophans on an almost straight vertical line, forty-eight ribs around the wall, and twenty-six parallel strands at a cap barrel. No skew, tilt, spiral or helical offset of a chain against the long axis is reported for any species by any means. The angles reported are other quantities: a cap flatness angle of approximately 34° against approximately 52° at a human comparison; approximately 3° between the two halves; 16° of wall curvature difference at an added-repeat variant; approximately 2° of cap rotation with a 10 Å cap lift between two conformations of one recombinant particle; and approximately 80° rising past 97° between neighbouring first repeats at a proposed opening. Handedness arrives differently at each account. At a 9 Å shell the enantiomer was assigned during model building, the account saying that at that resolution the analysis would not identify the true phase set. The 3.5 Å crystal accounts say nothing of handedness. A 13.5 Å reconstruction of an engineered particle could not establish handedness, and reconstructions at 38-fold and 40-fold did not resolve it. Recent human, rabbit and within-cell accounts report no handedness determination and open from earlier models with symmetry imposed. At one prokaryotic homolog account the ab initio maps did not distinguish the particle from its mirror image, refinement opened from a 20 Å smoothened shell of a predicted model, handedness was confirmed by fitting ideal alpha-helices against their mirror images, and predicted whole-particle handedness was kept where it agreed with a human vault account.

No eukaryotic vault account reports a buried waist interface area; approximately 225 Å² at a prokaryotic homolog and approximately 420 Å² at a human comparison stand at one account's own calculation of both, with none of the lining residues shared between them. The folding buffer is 100 mM sodium phosphate at pH 7.0 at one place and pH 6.5 to 7.0 with 50 to 100 mM sodium chloride, 1.5 mM magnesium chloride and 27 to 400 mM residual urea at another, with a third buffer of 20 mM phosphate at pH 6.6 and 50 mM sodium chloride beside them; protein at 1.8 to 8 in the units printed, at 22 °C and then at 4 °C for one to two days. items.section: 9.2 Clean cuts — where biology reports no problem
items.text: Mice with the major vault protein gene disrupted are viable, born at Mendelian ratios, breed normally, carry no clear physical abnormality to 16 months, and carry no microscopic difference at lung, liver or gastrointestinal tract and none at bone marrow or peripheral blood counts. The disruption is checked by absent transcript on Northern blot, absent protein on Western blot, and absent barrel-shaped particles by electron microscopy of purified liver fractions. Across twelve cytostatic agents no statistically significant difference in half-maximal inhibitory concentration stands between disrupted and unmodified embryonic stem cells, with doxorubicin at 7.28 ± 1.0 against 6.15 ± 0.77 ng/ml, etoposide at 2.38 ± 0.08 against 2.0 ± 0.08 ng/ml and vincristine at 0.86 ± 0.2 against 0.83 ± 0.053 ng/ml. Immature bone marrow carries no difference, doxorubicin at 0.131 ± 0.026 against 0.119 ± 0.027 µg/ml. Twenty-one unmodified against twenty-three disrupted mice given a single intravenous doxorubicin dose carry similar weight loss and recovery and similar white-cell decline with recovery by day 8, and five against five carry similar liver and ileum damage. At a resistant lung-cancer cell line, lowering the protein alters neither doxorubicin's departure from the nucleus nor drug sensitivity, and raising it at sensitive cells confers no resistance. Beside this, disrupted mice are more susceptible to Pseudomonas aeruginosa, and the protein is recruited to lipid rafts after infection, the maximal recruitment depending on bacterial binding to a chloride channel. A cell-free nuclear assembly system reports pore insertion requiring the protein. The particles stand at ten thousand to ten million per cell. Function is said unresolved at the field's own accounts across three decades. Vault absence from a nematode, a fly, a budding yeast and a mustard plant rests on a homology search the reporting account calls cursory together with earlier literature, and that same account says the protein's distribution beyond deuterostomes is too distant for direct homology search with available means, so absence and undetectability by that search do not part.
